boundary_profile.name: Site day — 17 Jan 2025
boundary_profile.detail: 17 January 2025, the most typical day of the fortnight: nearest the fortnight's medians in entering-water means and swings, load and flows (score 1.64; mean load 56 %): condenser water 28.43 to 30.13 °C, mean 28.95. Entering chilled and condenser water are taken straight from the export, one point every 10 minutes. Nothing is smoothed.

severity_anchor.standard: ASHRAE RP-1043 undercharge levels, 10/20/30/40 % charge loss, as milestones

rate_class.label: Moderate
rate_class.description: A breach large enough to be losing charge visibly over a shift, at about 5 % an hour. Typical of a gasket that has started to fail or a seal that has lost its face.

location.label: High side — discharge gas
location.description: Hot gas escapes at condensing pressure. It sees the same pressure as a liquid-side leak but is far less dense, so the same hole loses charge several times more slowly. Worth separating from the liquid case: a discharge leak is a different repair, and it develops slowly enough that it is often found by oil loss rather than by performance.
service_points: oil separator and its return line
pressure-relief piping on the discharge side

rate_class.label: Moderate
rate_class.description: A breach large enough to be losing charge visibly over a shift, at about 5 % an hour. Typical of a gasket that has started to fail or a seal that has lost its face.

severity_anchor.note: orifice sized to the rate class at the design point; it opens over the first 15 % of the time-to-40 %-loss and then holds, and the charge drains on the physics until protection trips

fault_definitions.name: Refrigerant leak (discharge gas)
fault_definitions.mechanism: A leak on the discharge side loses hot gas rather than liquid. It sees the full condensing pressure, like a liquid-side leak, but the escaping fluid is some thirty times less dense, so the same orifice drains the machine several times more slowly. Charge falls without the sharp collapse of condenser level and subcooling that marks a liquid leak, which is what makes the two worth separating: the machine loses capacity while its high side still looks close to normal, and the fault is often found by oil loss rather than by performance.

signature.note: liquid holdup drains, but later than a liquid leak
level control opens to defend the barrel

fault_definitions.severity_label: A major discharge-side breach: 60 mm^2 equivalent orifice
